questions_and_answers.question_text: When does summer vacation start and end for Chinese high schools?
Where does Yà come from, and what does zhōu mean?
What is the literal meaning of guójiā?
What does Zěnme? mean, and what can change its implication?
What are xīn shèhuì and jiù shèhuì jargon for?
Write the Chinese for "an uncultured person."
Write the Chinese for "Hong Kong sure has a lot of social problems."
When is the bound word -guó used?

answers.answer_text: Only in certain phrases or compound words — guójiā is the word to use everywhere else.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Well, you've come here too!"

answers.answer_text: Zěnme, nǐ yě dào zhèr lái le!

questions_and_answers.question_text: How do you say "in society" in Chinese?

articles.text:
5. A: Shǔjiàde shíhou, nǐ xiǎng dào  Where do you want to go over
      nǎr qu wánrwanr?                summer vacation?
   B: Wǒ xiǎng dào Yàzhōu jǐge       I'd like to go visit a few
      guójiā qu kànkan.               countries in Asia.

6. A: Zěnme, nǐ xiǎng yánjiū         Oh? Do you want to do research on
      Yàzhōude wénhuà chuántǒng?      Asia's cultural tradition?
   B: Bù néng shuō yánjiū. Wǒ zhǐ    It can't be called research. I just
      shi xiǎng qù kànkan nàlide      want to go have a look at the
      shèhuì qíngkuàng.               social situation there.

Notes on No. 5

shǔjià: "summer vacation." In China, summer vacation starts in August and ends in September for high schools; college ends in June and starts in late August.

Yàzhōu: "Asia." Yà comes from the transliterated word for Asia, Yàxìyà. Zhōu means "continent."

guójiā: "country, nation, state," literally, "country-family." The bound word -guó is used only in certain phrases or compound words. Guójiā is the word to use everywhere else.

Notes on No. 6

Zěnme?: "oh?; what?; really?" The intonation can change the implication.

Zěnme, nǐ yě dào zhèr lái le!    Well, you've come here too!
Zěnme? Tā bú shi Zhōngguo rén?   What? He's not Chinese? Then how is
Nà tāde Zhōngwén zěnme zhème     his Chinese so good?
hǎo ne?

wénhuà: "culture, civilization." Also "education, cultural background," as in méiyou wénhuàde rén, "an uncultured person."

shèhuì: "society; social." Xīn shèhuì and jiù shèhuì are jargon for the new and old societies (after and before the socialist transformation). "In society" is more often zài shèhuìshang.

Xiānggǎngde shèhuì wèntí zhēn    Hong Kong sure has a lot of social
duō.                             problems.
